contract: Compare complete UTF-8 conversions for every single byte, every byte pair in the multibyte profiles, and seeded streams. The ASS decoder exposes the visible string. Public glibc iconv supplies complete bytes after NUL and the first refused sequence's byte offset; the worker checks the visible prefix against ASS when present.
The exact differential byte and pair results in reviewed-mappings.tsv identify the strict-profile mapping exceptions observed on AArch64. Every compared matrix is retained with its reference fold.

pending_module_requirements: Historical Unicode Big5 differs from glibc Big5, including byte 80 (candidate refusal, reference U+0080) and the alternative mappings in the pair matrix. The seeded streams exercise these Unicode mapping differences.
At 815F the historical Unicode Shift-JIS table returns U+005C and glibc returns U+FF3C.
Strict EUC-KR follows the CP949 A1–FE table and ASCII. glibc also converts C1 bytes 80–9F and A2E8 to U+327E; strict-only pairs and offset differences remain visible in the ordered matrix.
Microsoft CP932 table 2.01 refuses the 1,880 F040–F9FC user codes which glibc maps to U+E000–U+E757, skipping trail 7F.
At A2E8 both CP949 conversions refuse the input, at offset zero in the candidate and offset two through glibc.
Microsoft CP950 table 2.01 differs from glibc CP950, including byte 80, vendor code assignments and strict refusals. The corpus retains the seeded streams accepted on only one side.
At A2E8 the C1-only EUC-KR profile refuses the pair and glibc 2.39 returns U+327E.
